text: To the Cave of Five Hundred Eyes.
When will your companions realize I know what I'm talking about
when I say it's dangerous to wander about at night?
First Barbara, now the Doctor goes off taking Susan and Pinchot with him.
All right, Marco, you can be angry later.
Let's get to this cave. Do you know where it is?
It must be your imagination, child. His eyes didn't move. It's corpse.
I saw them move, Grandfather. I swear I did.
If you must know, sir, we are looking for Miss Wright.
Why would she be in this cave?
I think this is your answer. We found it.
It is not wise to remain in these caves.
They are possessed with evil spirits.
Leave before the spirits are angered.
This man thinks this cave is haunted.
Susan saw the eyes and one of the faces move.
Do not strike them down, great spirits of Hashashin.
Do you want us to look now?
Well, what are you looking for, Chesterton?
She did see the eyes move.
Don't rubbish, rubbish, rubbish. What proof have you?
I've just seen them move myself.
Look, these eyes you see here have been set in from behind.
There must be some sort of a room behind this rock face.
And all we need now is to find out how to open it.
They played dice to see who killed Ian.
We were just in time, Jugana.
A moment or two later, and she would have been killed.
Why not let them go on their way?
My conscience does not permit it.
Look, I took their caravan away from them.
The least I can do is see them safely on their way home.
Do you think they hold you in such esteem?
The doctor, no, with good reason.
Has not that cunning Susan already won Pinchot from your side?
They will set us at each other's throats by lies and deceit.
And then, when they have divided us, then they will destroy us one by one.
They possess a caravan that flies.
What power they have is locked inside it, and I have the key.
This very evening, Marco, when we were out looking for this Barbara,
Chencho thought the old man was in his room.
He was out there with his caravan.
I'm saying that does a magician need a key to open a door?
You realize you're most fortunate to be alive?
Why did you go to the cave?
You know my rule about obtaining permission to leave here?
You were there when I arrived.
I have only been there once.
Mark well all that I have said.
You will remove your belongings to another room.
From this night on, you will not share with Susan again.
Yet what alternative had I but to separate them?
Now my caravan seethed with suspicion and discontent as we journey southwest.
The route takes us to the ancient cities of Suchao and Canchao, where the great wall of Cathay begins.
Following the wall, we travel south to Lanchao, which lies on the banks of the Yellow River.
Here, our route swings north, and with the river always in sight, we journey towards Shangri-La.
The problem is that Polo's change of attitude has slowed down my progress on the circuit.
I think you have done brilliantly to make any progress at all, Doctor.
How much longer do you think you will need?
Well, a bit more time and a lot of luck, I should say, about another night.
The following evening will even be better.
And that's when we say goodbye to Marco Polo.
Yes, and a jolly good riddance.
Well, I shall be jolly glad to leave here.
In fact, the only regrets I will have will be for Susan.
Oh, I think she and Ping Chao are very fond of each other.
It's a pity they've been kept apart so much.
It's a pity there was any association at all.
That Chinese child makes me nervous.
She found out about the key.
Yes, on the night that Barbara was captured.
Susan and Ping Chao thought Barbara had gone down to the cave and met with an accident,
so they came looking for me, just as I was about to enter the TARDIS.
It was then Ping Chao saw the key.
For me, this journey, in spite of all the dangers,
is the happiest time of my life.
What did Togana say to make Mr. Marco change so much?
A hundred times, but he remained silent.
If only we could find out.
If only we could prove that Togana had seen the cave of 500 eyes before.
It won't make much difference soon.
Your grandfather must have nearly finished the work in your caravan by now.
Will you say goodbye to me before you leave?
Even if it is very late.
No matter what time of night it is.
I've forgotten you knew anything about the key.
For the past three days, I have followed the course of the Yellow River
as it flows north of the small town of Hsinchu,
which lies nestled against the Great Wall.
Yes, it's in the passageway outside your door.
I want to go into town.
Why have I not thought of it before?
Mr. Marco, do you remember Togana's reply
when Miss Wright said she had followed him to the cave of 500 eyes?
He said he'd never been there before.
You bring a very serious charge, Pinchot.
When he came into the cave, Susan's grandfather showed him Miss Wright's handkerchief,
saying we had found it over there,
and the old lord pointed to a dark corner of the cave.
Now, do you remember what he said?
He asked if we had found it in the passageway.
If he had never been to the cave before,
how could he know that the dark corner was the passageway?
And on these grounds, you dare to call the warlord Togana a liar?
How dare you make such a reckless accusation?
Believe me, it will take much more than this to shake my confidence in Togana.
You should have killed them all when you...
the caravan sets out to cross the bamboo forests.
I shall signal you with a burning torch.
And then you will move in and slaughter them all,
He will send that on to Nogai,
whilst I will continue on to Shantou with...
I should let Polo die like an old woman in her bed.
With a stake through the heart.
I want a sign of him.
He must be in his room.
Be able to turn the tables on Togana.
Marco, I was just coming to have a word with you.
Well, I should have thought that was pretty obvious.
And tell me, why separate Susan and Ping Cho?
Oh, you can't really mean that.
Ping Cho's first loyalty is to me.
Yet she backed you against Togana.
Perhaps that's because we were telling the truth.
Let me tell you something, Ian.
Togana is a special emissary of Nogai,
on his way to talk peace with Kublai Khan.
You are mysterious travelers from some far-off land.
Now, if you were in my position, a servant of Kublai Khan,
I should keep an open mind.
I have something rather interesting to show you.
The old magician is in his caravan.
Well, why don't we go outside and have a look?
All we can do now is wait for him to come out.
This you are prepared to do?
If it'll convince you that Togana is making trouble,
we can wait here all night?
that when the warlord Togana says it is so,
I'm sorry I doubted your word, Togana.
You're an old man, and I do not wish to use force.
That is what you'll precisely have to do, Polo.
Did I not say he had another key?
Put that key in the lock, Polo.
And you will destroy the ship.
Then where will your oppressors Khan be, hmm?
You need more than a key to enter my ship.
I'd let you wreck it fast.
I wear the gold seal of Kublai Khan.
And by the authority it invests in me,
I do hereby seize and hold your caravan in his name.
Any resistance to this decree is instantly punishable by death.
How convinced which of us makes trouble?
What a nightmare this journey has become.
Our progress is impeded because Togana, the bearers, and I
must constantly be on the alert for any signs of trouble from the prisoners.
And Ping Chou's resentment of me only serves to make my task more difficult.
But I have succeeded in keeping her away from them
by setting up a separate tent for the doctor and his companions.
Born like this, we must get out!
I know the odds are against us, but at least we've got to try.
Yes, I quite agree with you.
The ship's waiting outside with the circuit finished and installed.
Grandfather Ping Chou wouldn't tell me about the second key.
Oh, don't worry about that now.
We must concentrate on getting one of those keys back.
Yes, and the only way I can see it is that we shall have to capture Polo.
At night, we've got the edge on them.
They've only got one guard, remember?
Yes, but how are you going to disarm him?
How are we going to get out of here?
And remember, that guard is out there watching for us.
As soon as I've dealt with that guard, I'll come back for you.
Grandfather, I suppose I think Mr. Markle won't give him the keys.
I think by the time I've finished with that gentleman, he'll only be too glad to let us go.
